title: kernel/mouse.inc's cursor half (cur_*): save-under, lazy cursor, shapes, busy cursor, multi-display move
summary: The 1bpp cursor (cur_move_mono, cur_put_mono/cur_get_mono, cur_geom) is excellent: one write a byte, geometry banked once, shape tables asserted at build time. The lazy-hide protocol is safe in every shipped arm, but it is opt-out and its proof instrument was never committed (mc-9). Verified findings: kern_big's VGA pointer is 21,450 cycles a packet and erase-then-draw, already queued as KHP_VGASAVE (mc-3). The SDK, vga12 and SPEC 7 still say gfx_lock hides the cursor, and raw framebuffer writers have no way to spend the promise (mc-5). [cur_dirty] is write-only (-~28 bytes, mc-1). kbm_move's gate lacks FPG_ARMED (mc-2). The rows=0 guards are dead (-24; the borrow framing was corrected, since it is equally unreachable, mc-4). The volume popup double-writes on a move (mc-6). A dead `mov si, bx` (mc-7). 21 doc fixes were confirmed. Withheld: the os88api.inc fix (abilock fingerprint), the cur_dirty SPEC lines (accurate until mc-1 lands) and two items the doc pass had already applied.

strengths.title: Each byte written once on 1bpp, decided once a move
strengths.why: The overlap is reduced to one row run and a 6-bit code before either walk, so neither walk tests per byte. Two save buffers are swapped arithmetically. Equivalence was proved over 36,000 random moves.

strengths.title: One place turns a position into an address
strengths.why: cur_geom alone subtracts the display origin and the hot spot. Restores replay the banked [cur_off]/[cur_rows]/[cur_b1ok], so a save and its restore cannot disagree.

strengths.title: Shape tables assert their own invariants
strengths.why: CUR_ROW/CUR_SHAPE_END fail the build on width, height, or a black bit outside its white row. Each of these defects is otherwise invisible except on the glass.

strengths.title: A cheap one-way promise
strengths.why: CURUNLAZY inlines the already-spent test at 19 sites, so a hide that is not owed costs one compare.

strengths.title: Busy clock tied to the hold
strengths.why: gfx_unlock is the single exit, so no caller can leave a clock on screen. The three pointer states each get an explicit arm.

strengths.title: Multi-display by not straddling
strengths.why: The arrow leaves one card whole and arrives on the other whole, so the fused loop never meets a seam. mou_clamp keeps the point inside some display.

strengths.title: cur_lazyrect is already per-output exclusion
strengths.why: Bands and damage fills ask about their own rect, which is the Win 3.x / ShieldCursor model, so R1 is an extension rather than a redesign.

findings.title: kern_big moves a VGA pointer through the generic rect machinery at IF=0: 21,450 cycles (about 4.5 ms) a packet, erase-then-draw
findings.detail: KHP_VGASAVE is defined only under KERN_MEGA (kernel.asm 293-294). On kern_big, cur_restoreu/cur_saveu are cur_rect + vga_restore_vram/vga_save_vram, called from the serial ISR before the EOI. LAST-DROP-PERF 7.1 row 3 measured cur_move at 21,450 cycles, against 15,100 with the knob. PERFORMANCE Part 5 quotes 15,100 without naming the kernel (SPEC 7.1.2 does name it). cur_move_1's planar arm is restore, then save, then draw, so overlap bytes show background between the passes (PREDICTED; never measured with m.flicker). About 20% of the CPU goes to the pointer during a sweep (PREDICTED; SPEC 7.1.2 measured 21.5% on the XT VGA).
findings.recommendation: Now: take KHP_VGASAVE on kern_big (+122 .vga, resident only on VGA/EGA machines; -6,350 cycles a packet). Take one m.flicker() pointer-sweep reading on os8088_xt_vga. Structural: rethink R2.
findings.verify_note: Re-read: KHP_VGASAVE sits inside %ifdef KERN_MEGA only; cur_move_1's GFX_VGA arm is cur_restoreu -> cur_geom -> cur_saveu -> cur_draw (erase-then-draw, its own comment says so). The finding is already queued as LAST-DROP-PERF row 3, so it is not new work. SPEC 7.1.2 measured the ISR's share as 21.5% (kern_big) -> 16.4%, which supports the ~20% prediction. The PERFORMANCE doc fix names the kernel; 11,500 against 12,000 is left alone (open question 2).

findings.title: The SDK and SPEC 7 say OSAPI_GFX_LOCK hides the cursor; since 7.1.4 it only promises to, and raw framebuffer writers have no way to make it happen
findings.detail: os88api.inc 220-221, the vga12.inc headers and SPEC.md 7's first bullet describe gfx_lock calling cursor_hide. The code only stores [cur_lazy]=1. Kernel primitives spend the promise. A package that writes the framebuffer itself inside the lock (outside FSX) has no API cell that spends it (cw_cur_unlazy and cw_cur_lazyrect are kernel-internal far shims, not OSAPI cells). Its writes then land under a lit arrow, and the next restore smears them. This is a contract defect, not a known live bug.
findings.recommendation: Now: correct the texts. vga12.inc and SPEC are in doc_fixes. os88api.inc's OSAPI_GFX_LOCK/UNLOCK comment is part of tools/abilock.py's fingerprint (an OSAPI %define's trailing comment is hashed), so that edit must land with `abilock.py --update` and no bump. It is NOT in doc_fixes, because applying it unchecked fails make. Record: an appended OSAPI_CUR_EXCLUDE(rect) cell that is cw_cur_lazyrect (INT 33h fn 10h / ShieldCursor).
findings.bytes_est: 0 now (docs); +5..+8 for the optional appended slot (record)
findings.prior_art: DOS INT 33h fn 10h conditional off; Mac ShieldCursor
findings.verify_note: gfx_lock .take ends with `mov byte [cur_lazy], 1` and no hide. gfx_unlock compares [cur_lazy] and either shows or calls cur_lazyend. grep of os88api.inc finds no unlazy or exclude cell. The os88api.inc fix was withheld from doc_fixes because abilock's surface() hashes the OSAPI_* define's comment (tools/abilock.py:85-91).

findings.title: The lazy-hide protocol is opt-out, and the instrument that proved it is not in the tree
findings.detail: SPEC 7.1.4's safety argument is a debug-build cell snapshot, and 7.1.1 calls that instrumentation never committed. GFXAUDIT counts unlocked draws and collisions, but not a cell written under a kept promise. CURLOG records events, but nothing in tools/ or tests/ reads cur_log. The defect class has recurred several times (7.1.5, the gfx_xor_rect and one-plane arms), each one found on the glass.
evidence: grep -ri cur_log tools tests: no reader
findings.recommendation: Under GFXAUDIT only: before a restore, recompute (save|white)&~black for each banked byte and compare it with VRAM. Log a mismatch to CURLOG with the tick and the interrupted CS:IP. Do it on 1bpp. Add a soak row that fails on a non-zero count.
findings.verify_note: SPEC 10847 does say '(instrumentation, never committed)'. The grep for cur_log/CURLOG over tools and tests hits only an unrelated win16spec file. The CURLOG_N comment's 'the CURLOG readers need no change' therefore names readers that do not exist.

findings.title: [cur_dirty] is written in six places and read in none
findings.detail: Stores: mou_apply .go (`mov byte [cur_dirty],0`) and .dirty (`,1`), cur_vis (`,0`), cur_lazyend (`,0`), kbm_move .pset (`mov [cur_dirty],al` plus its `mov al,1`/`mov al,0`). Nothing in kernel/, drivers/, apps/, tools/ or tests/ loads or compares it. The catch-up is position-based.
findings.recommendation: Delete the variable and its stores. .go becomes `jmp cur_move`, .dirty's jumps retarget to .out, and kbm_move drops its AL loads and store. Re-check t_hotpar parity. The SPEC 7, 9.6 and 12.8.4 text then changes with it.
findings.bytes_est: ~-27..-29 resident (kern_big and kern_small, ESTIMATED from encodings)
findings.verify_note: grep -n cur_dirty over the tree shows stores only; nothing reads it as a word through a neighbour either (cur_drawn_x follows it and is read by name). Encodings: four 5-byte immediate stores, one 3-byte AL store, two 2-byte AL loads, the 1-byte variable, plus call+ret -> jmp at .go: about 28. SPEC 10691/13745/27726 say it is SET, which is true of the code, so those lines were NOT changed as doc mismatches. They change with the deletion.

findings.title: kbm_move's draw gate is the pre-12.8.4 two-condition gate (no FPG_ARMED)
findings.detail: mou_apply refuses to draw while the progress widget is armed (FIELD-NOTES 34). kbm_move.paint tests only [gfx_lock_flag] and [cur_level], then calls cur_move, whose working set is in the primitive union gfx_u. fpg_arm's own comment (fprog.inc 771-790) states that the bar can be composed with the mutex unheld, by a non-UI task (dsk_xfer from a wm_wake_disp dispatch), and that only IRQ4 needs shutting out. kbm_move is a second lock-free painter that comment does not count. It runs from osapi_mouse when [mou_ptr]=0 and from the UI task's own keypad path.
findings.recommendation: Add FPG_ARMED to kbm_move.paint (+7), or factor one gate shared with mou_apply so the next condition lands once.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed in code. The window is narrow: it needs a mouseless machine, the keypad pointer, and a lock-free fpg arm pre-empted mid-fill. The UI task's own kbm path is a likelier way in than the worker the reviewer names. FPG_ARMED is 5 bytes plus a 2-byte jne = +7; the shared-gate figure was not costed. Not in any byte or ABI queue.

findings.title: The cur_rows=0 guards protect a value cur_geom cannot produce
findings.detail: vid_apply homes the pointer, mou_clamp keeps it on a display, and cur_move_multi/cur_vis activate that display. So [cur_celly] < [vid_ch], and cur_geom's rows are always >= 1, as its own comment says (its out: line says 0..CUR_GH). Six walks still open with `or ch,ch / jz` (24 bytes shipped, +8 more in the KHP_VGASAVE arm). A borrow would clamp to 12 rows and write past the display, but the same invariants exclude it, so neither the zero case nor the borrow is reachable.
findings.recommendation: Delete the six guards (-24) and fix cur_geom's 'out: 0..CUR_GH'. Optionally clamp [cur_celly] to [vid_ch]-1 (~+10) as defence in depth. Net -14 with the clamp, -24 without.
findings.bytes_est: -24 resident without the clamp, ~-14 with it (ESTIMATED)
findings.verify_note: The six shipped guards and the two KHP guards are as stated, at 4 bytes each. Corrected the framing: the 'dangerous borrow' is excluded by the same vid_apply/mou_clamp invariant that excludes rows=0, and vid_ch is the active display's extent, which cur_move_multi/cur_vis activate. So this is a size item, not a hazard. The clamp is optional hardening, not a fix. Note: cur_move_mono's comment at 5762 leans on CH being 0 after the background walk, which holds without the guard (dec ch to 0).

findings.title: ui_volume_service moves the pointer as cursor_hide + cursor_show (the pre-7.1.2 double write)
findings.detail: The volume popup's AL=2 poll moves the arrow with .move: cursor_hide, then .show: cursor_show. Two walks means the overlap bytes are written as background and then as arrow, on every adapter: FIELD-NOTES 6's wash-out, for the length of the popup.
findings.recommendation: Move it through cur_move under pushf/cli, as kbm_move does, so it is one fused walk.
findings.verify_note: ui.inc .poll -> .move: call cursor_hide; jmp .show -> call cursor_show. The reviewer's suggestion to call into cur_lazyend's tail was not checked against that routine's preconditions. A pushf/cli + cur_move pair is the shape kbm_move already uses.

findings.title: `mov si, bx` before cur_lazyck in wm_clip_set is dead
findings.detail: Neither arm of cur_lazyck reads SI on entry: the default loads [wm_clipwin], and CURFIX walks wm_clip_tab. wm_clip_set exits through kret_si anyway.
findings.recommendation: Delete it. SPEC 7.1.4's 'It takes the window in SI' is in doc_fixes.
findings.verify_note: The default arm pushes SI and then does `mov si, [wm_clipwin]`. The CURFIX arm reads wm_clip_tab/[wm_clip_n]. Not in KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE.

findings.title: The multi-display cursor pays full context swaps from the ISR
findings.detail: cur_move_multi calls vid_ctx_act twice per packet (three times on a seam jump), and cur_vis does the same pair on every show. vid_ctx_act short-circuits only when the display is already current. A swap is a 16-word copy plus its tail. About +1,000-1,500 cycles at IF=0 per packet, PREDICTED.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: vid_ctx_act opens with `cmp al, [vid_cur] / je .out`, so the cost is paid only when the last primitive left the other display current, as stated.

findings.title: Per-output rect exclusion at the unclipped entries (Win 3.x driver exclusion / QuickDraw ShieldCursor)
findings.detail: Any unclipped foreground primitive spends the hide wherever the arrow is. cur_lazyrect already takes an inclusive rect and preserves registers. A rect test at the GFXCLIP unclipped entries keeps one hide/show per hold. The deciding constraint is SPEC 7.1.4.3/7.1.4.4: a kept promise with a moving hand freezes the arrow, so CURFIX's motion gate must come with it.
findings.recommendation: Record as the 7.1.4.5.1 'change worth costing', with the CURFIX dependency and the owner's eye test stated.
findings.prior_art: Windows 3.x display-driver cursor exclusion; Mac QuickDraw ShieldCursor
findings.verify_note: Spot-check: cur_lazyrect exists with a rect contract, and 7.1.4.4 does make CURFIX off by default on the owner's eye test. Plausible as a record. The byte figure is unverified.

findings.title: Planar save-under in off-screen VRAM, moved by write-mode-1 latch copies
findings.detail: Mode 12h leaves 27,136 bytes a plane off-screen (65,536 - 38,400). A latch-based save, patch and compose would write each screen byte once with all four planes in one store, removing the erase-then-draw window. About 6,500 cycles, PREDICTED.
findings.recommendation: Record. First audit off-screen VRAM users (menu save-under, hibernate, themes) and the EGA memory probe.
findings.prior_art: Windows 3.x EGA/VGA driver off-screen pointer save area
findings.verify_note: The arithmetic checks. Record only; the cycle and byte figures are unverified predictions.

findings.title: Draw the cursor after the EOI, coalesced (the Mac VBL cursor task)
findings.detail: Fold into isr-7 R: re-read the position until it is stable, and state the gfx_u rule as 'no primitive in flight' rather than 'lock free'.
findings.verify_note: Not re-derived. It is already carried by isr-7 R. The gfx_u comment fix in doc_fixes states the inxfer exception.
